Solution skeleton:
- Statement: a sequence of (possibly dependent) random variables (X₁,…,X_ℓ′) over {0,1}^b is (ε,δ)-hitting if for every (target) set T ⊆ {0,1}^b with |T| ≥ ε·2^b, Pr[∃i ∈ {1,…,ℓ′} such that Xᵢ ∈ T] ≥ 1−δ. Note the two quantifiers: worst-case over T (the sequence must serve all dense targets simultaneously), and probability over the sequence only.
- Seed accounting. Independent sampling: ℓ′ samples, each uniform over {0,1}^b, need ℓ′·b bits. Expander walk on the 2^b-vertex graph of degree d: the seed encodes the start vertex v₀ (b bits) plus ℓ′−1 step indices i₁,…,i_ℓ′−1 ∈ {1,…,d} (log₂d bits each); total b + (ℓ′−1)·log₂d. For constant d this is b + O(ℓ′), versus b·ℓ′ for independence: the marginal cost of an extra sample is log₂d = O(1) bits instead of b bits, so the saving grows linearly with b. (Equivalently: independence is a random walk on the clique of size 2^b, whose 'degree' log is b bits per step.)
- Role of the graph structure. The saving is worthless unless the walk behaves like independent sampling for hitting, and that is a spectral fact: Theorem 5.5 bounds the probability of staying inside any W of density ρ by ρ(ρ + (1−ρ)λ/d)^(ℓ′−1), which is strong exactly when λ/d is small. On the disjoint union of two d-regular cliques, adjacency eigenvalues are ±d and d, so λ = d: the bound degenerates to 1 (no guarantee). Indeed a walk starting in the first clique can never reach a target set contained in the second clique — hitting fails outright. The condition λ < d is precisely what excludes such bottlenecks, so the spectral definition of expander is the hypothesis that makes the walk useful. ∎

Solution skeleton:
- Fix T with |T| = τ·2^b where τ = |T|/2^b ≥ ε. Since X₁,…,X_ℓ′ are independent and uniform over {0,1}^b,
  Pr[∀i: Xᵢ ∉ T] = ∏ᵢ Pr[Xᵢ ∉ T] = (1 − τ)^ℓ′ ≤ (1 − ε)^ℓ′,
  where independence gives the factorization into a product and uniformity gives Pr[Xᵢ ∉ T] = 1 − |T|/2^b = 1 − τ for every i.
- Therefore Pr[∃i: Xᵢ ∈ T] = 1 − Pr[∀i: Xᵢ ∉ T] ≥ 1 − (1 − ε)^ℓ′, and since T was arbitrary subject to |T| ≥ ε·2^b, the sequence is (ε,δ)-hitting for δ = (1 − ε)^ℓ′. (If |T| is larger, the bound only improves; the worst case is a set of density exactly ε, for which the inequality is an equality.)
- Where independence is used: in replacing the joint event by the product ∏ᵢ Pr[Xᵢ ∉ T]. If the samples are dependent, the factorization fails; the extreme case X₁ = X₂ = ⋯ = X_ℓ′ (perfect correlation) has miss probability 1 − τ ≥ 1 − ε, independent of ℓ′ — no exponential decay in the number of samples at all. The hitting problem asks for a sequence that keeps the exponential decay (1 − ε)^ℓ′ — or nearly so, δ = (1−(1−λ/d)·ε)^ℓ′ — while paying far fewer than ℓ′·b random bits; the expander walk is exactly such a sequence. ∎

Solution skeleton:
- (a) The class of distinguishers is the aspect that is fixed at an extremely weak level: the generator claims to fool only hitting tests — statistical tests that check whether at least one sample lies in a given set of density ≥ ε (Definition 5.4). The stretch measure is then generous (ℓ′ blocks of b bits from b + (ℓ′−1)·log₂d seed bits) and the generator runs in polynomial time — but both are easy to afford because the observers are so weak.
- (b) Unconditionality: the only ingredients are (1) an explicit (d,λ)-expander family — a combinatorial object whose existence and explicit constructibility are theorems, with no unproven assumption, and (2) Theorem 5.5, a purely mathematical bound on random walks. No one-way functions (Module 4), no hardness of E (Module 6): the guarantee that dense sets are hit with probability 1−δ holds as an unconditional mathematical fact.
- (c) Bullet comparison:
  - Distinguisher class: NW fools all circuits of size 2^{k/O(1)} (still a strong, assumption-worthy class); the expander walk fools only hitting tests (a very weak class).
  - Generator resources: NW may run 2^{O(k)} time — more than the distinguishers it fools, which is allowed and even necessary in the derandomization instantiation; the expander-walk generator runs in polynomial time, easily at least as fast as any hitting test.
  - Stretch: NW stretches k bits to 2^{k/O(1)} bits; the walk stretches b + (ℓ′−1)·log₂d bits to ℓ′·b bits (ℓ′·b vs. seed length — a polynomial factor, not exponential).
  - Assumption: NW is conditional — it assumes E has (almost-everywhere) exponential circuit complexity; the expander walk is unconditional.
  - Resource orientation: in the general-purpose setting the distinguisher is more complex than the generator; in NW and in the special-purpose settings (expander walks included) this relation is relaxed or reversed — the price of strong distinguisher classes is assumptions, and the currency for buying back unconditionality is weakening the observers.
- Bottom line: the same three-aspect template from Module 1 organizes every generator in the course; the special-purpose tools show that whenever one settles for a weak class of observers, explicit unconditional constructions appear — and the expander walk is the most striking example, since it simulates independence itself rather than merely producing independent-looking coordinates. ∎
